page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a total of 192 GB of VRAM. The server is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processor configured with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 2.2 GHz. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core or parallelized performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, multi-core capabilities are strong, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark extended instructions testing ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 4211.44 GB/sec. Most notably, the server excels in LLM inference, achieving top-tier (top 10%) performance in prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, as well as text generation for medium (7B) models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-96 offers high resource density for GPU-accelerated workloads, making it a viable alternative to more expensive A100 or H100 instances for specific inference tasks. However, users face a tradeoff: while parallelized GPU and multi-core CPU tasks perform exceptionally well, single-threaded operations (such as gzip compression and single-core text processing) are relatively weak. Additionally, the lack of bundled local storage requires external block storage provisioning, which may impact overall I/O-heavy workloads.

This server configuration is highly suited for large-scale machine learning inference, particularly large language model (LLM) prompt processing and text generation. It is also well-suited for multi-threaded compute tasks, video transcoding, and parallelized graphics rendering. It is less optimal for single-threaded applications or database workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized server designed for high-density GPU workloads. It features eight NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs with 192 GB of total VRAM, paired with 96 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (48 physical cores) running at 2.2 GHz and 384.0 GB of system memory. While single-core CPU performance and single-threaded operations are relatively weak, the instance delivers strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory bandwidth. Most notably, it achieves top-tier results in LLM inference prompt processing and text generation. Lacking local storage, this server is highly optimized for parallelized GPU-accelerated tasks, machine learning inference, and multi-threaded compute workloads, offering a cost-efficient alternative to higher-end GPU instances for specific AI workloads.
